structured.approach: First I took the Data Engineering tasks from feat.tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. For each one I checked whether it needs any external access. I read every ap_pipeline module, ci.py and schedule.json, and searched the repository for secret, credential and environment-variable patterns; the search found nothing. I then compared what is required with what the tool:repo-access view says is granted (taken from the permission table, which is passed by reference only). Nothing is required and nothing is granted, so there is no gap and I raised no access request. A draft from an earlier run was already at the output path. I read it and replaced it with a complete clean version, which corrects a statement about what dq.py imports and removes a stray line of tool output. The step denies shell commands, so I used only Read, Grep, Glob and Write. No connector was needed.

claims.text: The Data Engineering lane owns TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in ap_pipeline. TSK-03 to TSK-08 belong to other lanes.
TSK-02 is a pure function with no I/O. TSK-01 builds on synthetic feed v3 rows, and feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding.
TSK-01 must not change ingest.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json.
The pipeline entry point run(csv_text) receives the feed as text and calls parse_feed, to_model and quality_report without opening a connection.
Ingestion parses CSV text in memory with the csv and io modules.
The transform imports only datetime, decimal and typing, and the data-quality report imports nothing.
The package version is 0.4.0, and TSK-01 owns the version step.
CI runs locally with a coverage minimum of 90.0 and reads no credential.
schedule.json contains only frequency daily, time 02:00 and timezone Asia/Kolkata, and references no credential.
No secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline, so there is no gap and no access request is raised.
The repository branches are main (released), dev (integration) and feature/<story>.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): schedule.json defines a daily run, but no input says which runtime executes it or whether that runtime needs a credential to read the production feed. Check again at DE-13 (owner: Data engineering lead).
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope for FEAT-ZD-48600. TSK-01 and TSK-02 in ap_pipeline need no secrets in development, dev or main, and the permission table grants none. There is no gap, so I raised no access request, and there is no excess access to revoke. All work uses synthetic data only. One non-blocking question remains: whether DE-13 scheduling will need a credential.
